clean.title: Which split a decision tree prefers
clean.body:
A decision tree picks split A, because it leaves purer groups. Gini impurity is 1 minus the sum of squared class shares; a lower value means a purer group, and 0 would mean every example in the group has one class.

| Split | Groups | Gini per group | Weighted Gini |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 3 and 1, 1 and 3 | 0.375 and 0.375 | 0.375 |
| B | 2 and 2, 2 and 2 | 0.5 and 0.5 | 0.5 |

```rh-diagram
{"version":1,"diagram":{"kind":"cycle","title":"Which split a decision tree prefers","steps":["Start","Change","Result"]}}
```

For split A each group has shares 0.75 and 0.25, so Gini = 1 - (0.5625 + 0.0625) = 0.375. For split B each group has shares 0.5 and 0.5, so Gini = 1 - (0.25 + 0.25) = 0.5, the largest value two classes can give.
